g2453.text: From Judah: it can be translated “Jew” or “Judean”, and the Berean Standard Bible usually has “Jew”. Of its 185 verses, 76 are in Acts and 67 in John; Matthew, Mark and Luke use it in 5, 6 and 5. Jews use it of themselves (“I am a Jew,” Acts 22:3), others use it of them (“You are a Jew,” John 4:9), and it is the title over Jesus on the cross (John 19:19). The uses range from favourable to hostile.

h3064.text: From Judah: “Jew” or “Judean”. The Hebrew Scriptures mostly say “Israel”; this word is in 69 verses, 46 of them in Esther, where Mordecai is “a Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin” (Esth 2:5) and “for the Jews it was a time of light and gladness” (Esth 8:16). It is also in Jeremiah, Nehemiah, 2 Kings, and Zechariah 8:23: “ten men from the nations … will tightly grasp the robe of a Jew.”

h3062.text: The Aramaic form, in Ezra (7 verses) and Daniel (2): “the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews” (Ezra 5:5), who built and prospered (Ezra 6:14); and “some astrologers came forward and maliciously accused the Jews” (Dan 3:8).
